claim: NFATc1 is a crucial regulator of articular, but not growth-plate, chondrocyte differentiation during development.
source: Here, we identified that the nuclear factor of activated T-cells cytoplasmic 1 (NFATc1) is a crucial regulator of articular, but not growth-plate, chondrocyte differentiation during development.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript, including lineage tracing, gene expression analysis, and functional studies.

claim: At embryonic day 13.5, NFATc1-expressing cells were mainly located in the flanking region of the joint interzone.
source: At the early stage of mouse knee development (embryonic day 13.5), NFATc1-expressing cells were mainly located in the flanking region of the joint interzone.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy images and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1.

claim: NFATc1-expressing cells generated almost all articular chondrocytes but not chondrocytes in limb growth-plate primordium.
source: With development, NFATc1-expressing cells generated almost all articular chondrocytes but not chondrocytes in limb growth-plate primordium.
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data in Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice showing GFP+ cells in articular cartilage but not growth plate.

claim: NFATc1-expressing cells displayed prominent capacities for colony formation and multipotent differentiation.
source: NFATc1-expressing cells displayed prominent capacities for colony formation and multipotent differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by ex vivo colony formation assays and differentiation assays shown in Figure 3.

claim: The expression of NFATc1 was diminished with articular chondrocyte differentiation.
source: Strikingly, the expression of NFATc1 was diminished with articular chondrocyte differentiation
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of lineage tracing in Nfatc1Cre and Nfatc1CreERT2 mice, and gene expression analysis during chondrogenesis.

claim: Suppressing NFATc1 expression in articular cartilage progenitors was sufficient to induce spontaneous chondrogenesis.
source: suppressing NFATc1 expression in articular cartilage progenitors was sufficient to induce spontaneous chondrogenesis
evidence: This claim is supported by CRISPR/Cas9 deletion experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Overexpressing NFATc1 suppresses chondrogenesis.
source: while overexpressing NFATc1 suppresses chondrogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by retroviral overexpression experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: NFATc1 negatively regulated the transcriptional activity of the Col2a1 gene.
source: Mechanistically, NFATc1 negatively regulated the transcriptional activity of the Col2a1 gene.
evidence: This claim is supported by CUT&RUN-qPCR and luciferase assays shown in Figure 5G-I.

claim: NFATc1 characterizes articular, but not growth-plate, cartilage progenitors during development.
source: Thus, our results reveal that NFATc1 characterizes articular, but not growth-plate, cartilage progenitors during development
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data showing NFATc1 expression in articular but not growth plate regions.

claim: NFATc1 negatively determines articular chondrocyte differentiation at least partly through regulating COL2A1 gene transcription.
source: negatively determines articular chondrocyte differentiation at least partly through regulating COL2A1 gene transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by mechanistic studies including CUT&RUN and luciferase assays demonstrating NFATc1 binding to and regulating Col2a1 promoter activity.

claim: GDF5 is one of the genes widely used for tracking synovial joint and articular cartilage development.
source: GDF5 is one of the genes widely used for tracking synovial joint and articular cartilage development Decker, 2017.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Gdf5-expressing cell lineages form almost all articular chondrocytes.
source: Using reporter mice, multiple groups have displayed that Gdf5-expressing cell lineages form almost all articular chondrocytes Koyama et al., 2008; Rountree et al., 2004; Shwartz et al., 2016; Decker et al., 2017.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: GDF5 expression is greatly diminished at the late stage of embryonic development and almost undetectable in articular cartilage in neonatal mice.
source: Also, GDF5 expression is greatly diminished at the late stage of embryonic development and almost undetectable in articular cartilage in neonatal mice Decker, 2017.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: PRG4 is an articular cartilage progenitor marker in the late stage of synovial joint development.
source: PRG4 is an articular cartilage progenitor marker in the late stage of synovial joint development Chijimatsu and Saito, 2019; Chagin and Medvedeva, 2017.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: PRG4 encodes lubricin, a major component of synovial fluid and responsible for joint lubricity.
source: This gene encodes lubricin, a major component of synovial fluid and responsible for joint lubricity Coles et al., 2010.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: PRG4 is detected from the stage of joint cavitation and is predominantly expressed in the surficial layer of developed articular cartilage.
source: PRG4 is detected from the stage of joint cavitation and is predominantly expressed in the surficial layer of developed articular cartilage Rhee et al., 2005.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: PRG4 was identified as a marker for postnatal and adult articular cartilage progenitors using Prg4CreERT2 reporter mice.
source: Several studies exploited Prg4CreERT2 reporter mice to track postnatal articular cartilage development and identified this gene as a marker for postnatal and adult articular cartilage progenitors Decker et al., 2017; Kozhemyakina et al., 2015.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: PRG4 does not label the primary progenitors of articular cartilage.
source: Since PRG4 starts to predominantly express and function at the late stage of articular cartilage development, it does not label the primary progenitors of articular cartilage.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the timing of PRG4 expression described in the manuscript.

claim: Sox9, Dkk3, and Tgfbr2 were utilized to track articular cartilage and synovial joint development.
source: Several other molecules, such as Sox9, Dkk3, and Tgfbr2, were also utilized to track articular cartilage and synovial joint development Shwartz et al., 2016; Decker et al., 2017; Li et al., 2013
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: None of Sox9, Dkk3, and Tgfbr2 have been shown to specifically and constantly label articular cartilage progenitors.
source: but none of these molecules have been shown to specifically and constantly label articular cartilage progenitors and to be able to distinguish the origin of articular chondrocytes.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the cited literature and the authors' assessment.

claim: SOX9 is essential in multiple steps of chondrogenesis.
source: SOX9 is essential in multiple steps of chondrogenesis, but it was originally and mainly studied in growth-plate chondrocytes Lefebvre and Dvir-Ginzberg, 2017.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: SOX9 is expressed in articular cartilage and is essential for maintaining adult articular cartilage homeostasis.
source: Although SOX9 is also expressed in articular cartilage and is essential for maintaining adult articular cartilage homeostasis Haseeb et al., 2021
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: SOX9 starts to express in mesenchymal cells from the very early stage of limb development before the cartilage template formation.
source: Also, SOX9 starts to express in mesenchymal cells from the very early stage of limb development before the cartilage template formation and it alone is not sufficient to induce chondrogenesis Lefebvre and Dvir-Ginzberg, 2017; Akiyama et al., 2005.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: SOX9 alone is not sufficient to induce chondrogenesis.
source: and it alone is not sufficient to induce chondrogenesis Lefebvre and Dvir-Ginzberg, 2017; Akiyama et al., 2005.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: NFATc1 is one of the five members of the NFAT family.
source: The nuclear factor of activated T-cells, cytoplasmic 1 (NFATc1) is one of the five members of the NFAT family, which share a similar DNA binding domain of approximately 300 amino acid residues Hogan et al., 2003; Vaeth and Feske, 2018.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents established knowledge.

claim: NFAT family members share a similar DNA binding domain of approximately 300 amino acid residues.
source: which share a similar DNA binding domain of approximately 300 amino acid residues Hogan et al., 2003; Vaeth and Feske, 2018.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents established knowledge.

claim: NFAT signaling plays a broad function in various physiological and pathological processes, including immune cell differentiation and functions, cardiac valve development, and cancer progression and metastasis.
source: NFAT signaling plays a broad function in various physiological and pathological processes, including immune cell differentiation and functions, cardiac valve development, and cancer progression and metastasis Hogan et al., 2003; Mancini and Toker, 2009.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: NFATc1 is critical for osteoclast differentiation and functions.
source: In the skeletal system, NFATc1 is critical for osteoclast differentiation and functions Aliprantis et al., 2008; Takayanagi, 2007
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: NFATc1 is involved in osteoblast differentiation by cooperating with the Osterix gene.
source: and is also involved in osteoblast differentiation by cooperating with the Osterix gene Koga et al., 2005.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: NFATc1 expression was found in the superficial layers of articular cartilage.
source: Intriguingly, NFATc1 expression was found in the superficial layers of articular cartilage as well and decreased in human osteoarthritic cartilage Greenblatt et al., 2013.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: NFATc1 expression decreased in human osteoarthritic cartilage.
source: and decreased in human osteoarthritic cartilage Greenblatt et al., 2013.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: NFATc1 has a function in restricting osteochondroma formation from entheseal progenitors.
source: Following these studies, we recently identified a function of NFATc1 in restricting osteochondroma formation from entheseal progenitors Ge et al., 2016
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: NFATc1 is a suppressor of chondrogenesis in entheseal progenitor cells.
source: revealing that NFATc1 is a suppressor of chondrogenesis in these cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the authors' previous work on entheseal progenitors.

claim: In Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ dual-fluorescence reporter mice, the majority of articular chondrocytes expressed GFP at 8 weeks of age (90.55 ± 6.38%, n=5 mice).
source: we unexpectedly found that in Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ dual-fluorescence reporter mice, the majority of articular chondrocytes expressed green fluorescence protein (GFP) at 8 weeks of age [Figure 1(A and B), 90.55 ± 6.38%, n=5 mice].
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal microscopy shown in Figure 1B.

claim: At E13.5, GFP+ cells were mainly localized to the flanking region of the joint interzone with only sporadic distribution in the interzone site.
source: At E13.5, GFP+ cells were mainly localized to the flanking region of the joint interzone with only sporadic distribution in the interzone site.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The localization of Nfatc1-expressing cells surrounding the joint interzone was verified after administering tamoxifen to Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice at E11.5 and sampling at E13.5.
source: The localization of Nfatc1-expressing cells surrounding the joint interzone was verified after administering tamoxifen to Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice at E11.5 and sampling at E13.5 [Figure 1—figure supplement 1A].
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In neonatal Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice (P0), GFP+ cells consisted of a portion of cells in the presumptive articular cartilage site.
source: In neonatal Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice (P0), GFP+ cells consisted of a portion of cells in the presumptive articular cartilage site [Figure 1A].
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1A.

claim: At 2 weeks of age, most articular chondrocytes were GFP+ in Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice.
source: Strikingly, at 2 weeks of age, most articular chondrocytes turned out to be GFP+, similar to that at 8 weeks of age [Figure 1(A)].
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1A.

claim: With tamoxifen pulse, RFP+ cells were found scattered in the articular cartilage at 2 weeks of age accounting for about 22.75 ± 2.18% (n=3 mice) of all cells of articular cartilage.
source: Of interest, with tamoxifen pulse, RFP+ cells were found scattered in the articular cartilage at 2 weeks of age accounting for about 22.75 ± 2.18% (n=3 mice) of all cells of articular cartilage
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26RFP/+ mice shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Most RFP+ cells were confined to the superficial layers of articular cartilage at 8 weeks of age (10.94 ± 1.26%, n=3).
source: while most RFP+ cells were confined to the superficial layers of articular cartilage at 8 weeks of age (10.94 ± 1.26%, n=3) [Figure 1(C and D)].
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data and confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: There were no GFP+ chondrocytes in the primordium of growth-plate cartilage at E13.5 in both Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ and tamoxifen-induced Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice.
source: Notably, there were no GFP+ chondrocytes in the primordium of growth-plate cartilage at E13.5 in both Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ and tamoxifen-induced Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice [Figure 1(A) and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A]
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: NFATc1-expressing cells do not generate the cartilaginous primordium of growth-plate.
source: suggesting that NFATc1-expressing cells do not generate the cartilaginous primordium of growth-plate.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the absence of GFP+ cells in growth plate primordium.

claim: There was no Cre leakage in the articular cartilage in Rosa26mTmG/+ control mice and Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice without tamoxifen induction.
source: We did not detect GFP+ cells in articular cartilage in Rosa26mTmG/+ control mice and Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice without tamoxifen induction [Figure 1—figure supplement 1D], suggesting that there was no Cre leakage in the articular cartilage in these two reporter mouse lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Many GFP+ articular chondrocytes in Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice at 2 weeks and 8 weeks of age were derived from Nfatc1-expressing progenitors and had lost the expression of NFATc1 with development.
source: Therefore, by mapping GFP and RFP expression in articular cartilage of Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ and Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26RFP/+ mice respectively [Figure 1—figure supplement 1C], many GFP+ articular chondrocytes in Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice at 2 weeks and 8 weeks of age should be derived from Nfatc1-expressing progenitors and had lost the expression of NFATc1 with development.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparing lineage tracing and real-time expression data.

claim: Local GFP+ cell clusters with 3–6 cells each could be observed in articular cartilage by 2 weeks and 8 weeks of age in Nfatc1CreERT2;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice after tamoxifen pulse at P0 and P1.
source: Local GFP+ cell clusters with 3–6 cells each could be observed in articular cartilage by 2 weeks and 8 weeks of age [Figure 2(A and B)].
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: GFP+ cell clusters were found in the meniscus, synovial lining, and ligament.
source: Notably, GFP+ cell clusters were also found in the meniscus, synovial lining, and ligament [Figure 2(A and B)]
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: NFATc1 marks progenitor cells for joint tissues other than articular cartilage.
source: suggesting that NFATc1 also marks progenitor cells for joint tissues other than articular cartilage.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of GFP+ cell clusters in multiple joint tissues.

claim: In Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice, GFP+ cells formed the meniscus, synovial lining, ligament, and primordium of the patella at the knee.
source: Indeed, in Nfatc1Cre;Rosa26mTmG/+ mice, GFP+ cells also formed the meniscus, synovial lining, ligament, and primordium of the patella at the knee [Figure 1(A) and Figure 2(C)].
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1A and Figure 2C.

claim: GFP+ cells formed remarkably more numerous and larger cell clones in comparison with GFP- cells when plated at the same cell densities and cultured for the same time period.
source: The ex vivo colony formation assay showed that GFP+ cells formed remarkably more numerous and larger cell clones in comparison with GFP- cells when plated at the same cell densities and cultured for the same time period [Figure 3(B)].
evidence: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A similar outcome of enhanced colony formation by GFP+ cells could be observed even after five consecutive cell passages.
source: A similar outcome could be observed even after five consecutive cell passages [Figure 3—figure supplement 1A].
evidence: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: NFATc1-expressing articular cartilage progenitors display a rigorous capacity for colony formation both in vivo and ex vivo.
source: Thus, NFATc1-expressing articular cartilage progenitors display a rigorous capacity for colony formation both in vivo and ex vivo.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the in vivo cell cluster formation and ex vivo colony formation assays.

claim: GFP+ cells displayed a much higher potential to differentiate toward chondrocytes, osteoblasts, and adipocytes compared to GFP- cells.
source: Notably, GFP+ cells displayed a much higher potential to differentiate toward chondrocytes, osteoblasts, and adipocytes compared to GFP- cells [Figure 3(C–E)].
evidence: This claim is supported by differentiation assay data shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: GFP+ cells have a more prominent capacity for proliferation and chondrogenesis compared to GFP- cells.
source: indicating that GFP+ cells have a more prominent capacity for proliferation and chondrogenesis compared to GFP- cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the pellet culture data showing larger pellets and more robust chondrogenesis in GFP+ cells.

claim: When transplanted with Matrigel matrix underneath the dorsal skin of SCID mice, GFP+ cells differentiated and formed typical chondrocytes as well as chondrocyte clusters within 4 weeks.
source: Furthermore, when transplanted alongside with Matrigel matrix underneath the dorsal skin of SCID mice, these GFP+ cells differentiated and formed typical chondrocytes as well as chondrocyte clusters within 4 weeks
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo transplantation data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The formation of chondrocytes was rarely observed when transplanting GFP- cells.
source: while the formation of chondrocytes was rarely observed when transplanting GFP- cells [Figure 3(F) and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B].
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo transplantation data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Many chondrocyte clusters from GFP+ cells had formed hypertrophic cartilage-like tissue with a certain hardness.
source: Notably, many chondrocyte clusters from GFP+ cells had formed hypertrophic cartilage-like tissue with a certain hardness, similar to the physiological process of articular cartilage development [Figure 3(F)].
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis of transplants shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Bioinformatics analysis identified 117 high- and 168 low-expressing genes in GFP+ vs. GFP- cells.
source: Bioinformatics analysis identified 117 high- and 168 low-expressing genes in GFP+ vs. GFP- cells [Figure 4—figure supplement 1A].
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: High-expressing genes in GFP+ cells were mainly related to skeletal system development, cartilage development, or extracellular matrix component and organization.
source: High-expressing genes in GFP+ cells were mainly related to skeletal system development, cartilage development, or extracellular matrix component and organization [Figure 4(B) and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B].
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: High-expressing genes in GFP+ cells included several previously reported articular cartilage progenitor cell markers such as Osr2, Prg4, Postn, Col3a1, Gdf6, and Tgfbr2.
source: Of note, these high-expressing genes in GFP+ cells included several previously reported articular cartilage progenitor cell markers Decker, 2017; Bian et al., 2020, such as Osr2, Prg4, Postn, Col3a1, Gdf6, and Tgfbr2 [Figure 4(C)].
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome analysis data shown in Figure 4C and citations to published literature.

claim: Enriched genes in GFP- cells were mainly relevant to muscle cell development and differentiation.
source: In contrast, enriched genes in GFP- cells were mainly relevant to muscle cell development and differentiation [Figure 4—figure supplement 1C]
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: GFP- single-clone cells could be skeletal muscle progenitors.
source: suggesting that GFP- single-clone cells could be skeletal muscle progenitors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the enrichment of muscle-related genes in GFP- cells.

claim: The characteristic molecular signature and enriched biological pathways in GFP+ cells were verified by the second transcriptome analysis using bulk primary GFP+ cells.
source: Importantly, the characteristic molecular signature and enriched biological pathways in GFP+ cells were verified by the second transcriptome analysis using bulk primary GFP+ cells [Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-F].
evidence: This claim is supported by a second independent transcriptome analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-F.

claim: Both GFP+ and GFP- progenitors expressed several surface markers of cells of mesenchymal origin, including Cd9, Sca1, Thy1, Cd73, Cd166, Cd200, and Cd51.
source: Transcriptome analyses showed that both GFP+ and GFP- progenitors expressed several surface markers of cells of mesenchymal origin, including Cd9, Sca1, Thy1, Cd73, Cd166, Cd200, and Cd51
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome analysis data.

claim: Both GFP+ and GFP- progenitors did not express hematopoietic or endothelial markers Cd11b, Cd45, or Cd31.
source: but not hematopoietic or endothelial markers Cd11b, Cd45, or Cd31 (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome analysis data.

claim: When compared with GFP- cells, GFP+ cells displayed higher expression of Cd105, Cd10, and Cd13 and lower expression of Cd146, Cd29, and Cd151.
source: When compared with GFP- cells, GFP+ cells displayed higher expression of Cd105, Cd10, and Cd13 and lower expression of Cd146, Cd29, and Cd151 [Figure 4(D)].
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome analysis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The expression of CD105, CD9, SCA1, CD166, CD200, CD11B, CD45, and CD31 were verified by flow cytometry in GFP+ and GFP- cells.
source: The expression of CD105, CD9, SCA1, CD166, CD200, CD11B, CD45, and CD31 were further verified by flow cytometry in GFP+ and GFP- cells [Figure 4(E and F) and Figure 4—figure supplement 2].
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E, F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The diminishment of Nfatc1 expression was detected in ex vivo chondrogenesis in Nfatc1-expressing articular cartilage progenitors.
source: Consistently, the diminishment of Nfatc1 expression was also detected in ex vivo chondrogenesis in Nfatc1-expressing articular cartilage progenitors [Figure 5(A)].
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis during ex vivo chondrogenesis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The deletion of NFATc1 expression in GFP+ articular cartilage progenitors by CRISPR/CAS9 was enough to induce chondrocyte differentiation without adding the chondrogenic medium.
source: Strikingly, the deletion of NFATc1 expression was enough to induce chondrocyte differentiation without adding the chondrogenic medium as shown by alcian blue staining and induced expression of Acan, Col2a1, and Col10a1 [Figure 5(B)].
evidence: This claim is supported by CRISPR/Cas9 deletion experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Overexpression of NFATc1 in GFP+ progenitor cells inhibited chondrocyte differentiation.
source: In the meantime, overexpression of NFATc1 in GFP+ progenitor cells inhibited chondrocyte differentiation [Figure 5(C) and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A].
evidence: This claim is supported by retroviral overexpression experiments shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The staining for articular cartilage was markedly strengthened in Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl (homozygous) vs. Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/+ (heterozygous) mice.
source: The staining for articular cartilage was markedly strengthened in Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl (homozygous) vs. Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/+ (heterozygous) mice [Figure 5(D and E)].
evidence: This claim is supported by histological staining shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: The expression of Acan, Col2a1, and Col10a1 genes was significantly upregulated in the articular cartilage of Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl mice.
source: Consistently, the expression of Acan, Col2a1, and Col10a1 genes was significantly upregulated in the articular cartilage of Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl mice [Figure 5(F)].
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative PCR data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The articular cartilage consisted of mostly round, large chondrocytes in Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl mice, instead of the normal transitional alignment from the superficial layer to the deep layers.
source: Notably, the articular cartilage consisted of mostly round, large chondrocytes in Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl mice, instead of the normal transitional alignment from the superficial layer to the deep layers [Figure 5(E)].
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The volume changes of articular chondrocytes resulted in an increased thickness of articular cartilage in Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl vs. Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/+ mice.
source: The volume changes of articular chondrocytes resulted in an increased thickness of articular cartilage in Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl vs. Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/+ mice [Figure 5(E)].
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The in vivo deletion of Nfatc1 in limb mesenchymal progenitors promotes articular chondrocyte differentiation.
source: These results indicate that the in vivo deletion of Nfatc1 in limb mesenchymal progenitors promotes articular chondrocyte differentiation as well.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the in vivo conditional knockout data in Prrx1Cre;Nfatc1fl/fl mice.

claim: Nfatc1 deletion in Col2a1-expressing cells (Nfatc1Col2a1 mice) does not affect articular cartilage integration or osteoarthritis progression induced by destabilization of the medial meniscus.
source: Note that a previous study showed that Nfatc1 deletion in Col2a1-expressing cells (Nfatc1Col2a1 mice) does not affect articular cartilage integration or osteoarthritis progression induced by destabilization of the medial meniscus Greenblatt et al., 2013
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: NFATc1 is dispensable in Col2a1-expressing differentiated articular chondrocytes.
source: suggesting that NFATc1 is dispensable in Col2a1-expressing differentiated articular chondrocytes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the cited study showing no effect of NFATc1 deletion in Col2a1-expressing cells.

claim: NFATc1 may primarily function in articular cartilage progenitors to regulate articular chondrocyte differentiation.
source: Therefore, NFATc1 may primarily function in articular cartilage progenitors to regulate articular chondrocyte differentiation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparing the effects of NFATc1 deletion in progenitors vs. differentiated chondrocytes.

claim: Col2a1 was one of the most significantly changed chondrocyte-related genes after deleting or overexpressing NFATc1.
source: Based on gene expression changes after deleting or overexpressing NFATc1, Col2a1 turned out to be one of the most significantly changed chondrocyte-related genes we examined [Figure 5(B, C and F) and reference Ge et al., 2016].
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5B, C, F and cited reference.

claim: Computational screening identified a total of 38 potential NFAT binding sites across the upstream 6 k base pairs of exon 1 and the intron 1 of mouse Col2a1 gene.
source: To understand the mechanism of NFATc1 regulating articular chondrocyte differentiation, we performed computational screening and identified a total of 38 potential NFAT binding sites across the upstream 6 k base pairs of exon 1 and the intron 1 of mouse Col2a1 gene [Figure 5(G)].
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: FIMO analysis identified a NFATc1 motif that locates in mouse chr15: 98004609–98004620 and overlaps with the Col2a1 promoter region.
source: To narrow down the NFATc1 binding sites in the regulatory region of the Col2a1 gene, we performed a FIMO analysis Grant et al., 2011 and identified a NFATc1 motif that locates in mouse chr15: 98004609–98004620 and overlaps with the Col2a1 promoter region [Figure 5—figure supplement 1B].
evidence: This claim is supported by FIMO analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and citation to the FIMO method.

claim: The binding of NFATc1 to the Col2a1 promoter region (chr15: 98004609–98004620) was verified using CUT&RUN.
source: Furthermore, we verified the binding of NFATc1 to this site using the technique of cleavage under targets and release using nuclease (CUT&RUN) [Figure 5(H)].
evidence: This claim is supported by CUT&RUN-qPCR data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: NFATc1 plays a role in regulating Col2a1 gene transcription.
source: These results show that NFATc1 might play a role in regulating Col2a1 gene transcription.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the computational and CUT&RUN data showing NFATc1 binding to Col2a1 regulatory regions.

claim: Silence or overexpression of NFATc1 markedly upregulated or downregulated the transcriptional activity of Col2a1, respectively.
source: Indeed, the luciferase analysis showed that silence or overexpression of NFATc1 markedly upregulated or downregulated the transcriptional activity of Col2a1, respectively [Figure 5(I)].
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: The interzone cells have been considered as the origin of articular chondrocytes.
source: For quite a long period, the interzone cells have been considered as the origin of articular chondrocytes Chijimatsu and Saito, 2019; Rux et al., 2019.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Progenitor cells in the flanking mesenchyme surrounding the joint interzone were found to migrate into the interzone region and form articular cartilage.
source: Also, progenitor cells in the flanking mesenchyme surrounding the joint interzone were found to migrate into the interzone region and form articular cartilage Shwartz et al., 2016; Decker et al., 2017; Niedermaier et al., 2005; Koyama et al., 2007.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The current obscurity in identifying the precise origin of articular chondrocytes could be attributed to the lack of a specific molecular marker to distinguish cells in the flanking region from interzone cells.
source: The current obscurity in identifying the precise origin of articular chondrocytes could be attributed to the lack of a specific molecular marker to distinguish cells in the flanking region from interzone cells.
evidence: This claim represents the authors' interpretation of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The limited expression of NFATc1 in the flanking region at the primary stage of mouse knee development provides a unique opportunity to track progenitors in the flanking region during articular cartilage development.
source: From this perspective, the limited expression of NFATc1 in the flanking region at the primary stage of mouse knee development [E13.5, Figure 1(A and E) and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A] provides a unique opportunity to track progenitors in the flanking region during articular cartilage development.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the spatial expression pattern of NFATc1 shown in the data.

claim: NFATc1-expressing progenitors in the flanking region may represent the origin of articular chondrocytes.
source: The progressive pattern of NFATc1-expressing cells contributing to articular cartilage formation (Figures 1–2) suggests that NFATc1-expressing progenitors in the flanking region may represent the origin of articular chondrocytes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the lineage tracing data showing progressive contribution of NFATc1+ cells to articular cartilage.

claim: NFATc1 can constantly track articular cartilage progenitors throughout embryonic development and postnatal growth.
source: Notably, these results also demonstrate that NFATc1 can constantly track articular cartilage progenitors throughout embryonic development and postnatal growth.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the lineage tracing data at multiple developmental stages.

claim: NFATc1-expressing articular cartilage cells enrich several previously identified articular cartilage progenitor cell markers including Osr2, Prg4, Postn, Col3a1, and Gdf6.
source: Transcriptome analyses in both single-clone and bulk primary cells reveal that NFATc1-expressing articular cartilage cells enrich several previously identified articular cartilage progenitor cell markers including Osr2, Prg4, Postn, Col3a1, and Gdf6 [Figure 4(C); Decker, 2017; Bian et al., 2020]
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome analysis data and citations to published literature.

claim: Cell surface molecules including CD105, CD13, CD10, CD9, SCA1, and CD166 can be considered as complementary markers for identifying and screening articular cartilage progenitors.
source: In addition, cell surface molecules including CD105, CD13, CD10, CD9, SCA1, and CD166 can be considered as complementary markers for identifying and screening articular cartilage progenitors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the transcriptome and flow cytometry data showing differential expression of these markers.

claim: NFATc1-expressing articular cartilage progenitors enrich a set of genes whose mutations have been linked to a diverse range of human musculoskeletal disorders.
source: Most impressively, NFATc1-expressing articular cartilage progenitors enrich a set of genes like Fbn2, Piezo2, Dchs1, Enpp1, Gdf6, Fgf9, Trps1, Col27a1, Tgfbr2, Col1a1, and Col1A2 [Figure 4(B)], whose mutations have been linked to a diverse range of human musculoskeletal disorders (https://www.omim.org).
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome data and reference to the OMIM database.

claim: The dysfunction of articular cartilage progenitors may underlie human musculoskeletal disorders associated with mutations in genes enriched in these progenitors.
source: These findings suggest that the dysfunction of articular cartilage progenitors may underlie these human musculoskeletal disorders.
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the enrichment of disease-associated genes in articular cartilage progenitors.

claim: Gdf5 is greatly diminished with synovial joint development and undetectable in the articular cartilage of neonatal mice.
source: Of note, we did not detect the expression of Gdf5 in articular cartilage progenitors from neonatal mice, which coincides with previous reports that Gdf5 is greatly diminished with synovial joint development and undetectable in the articular cartilage of neonatal mice Decker, 2017; Francis-West et al., 1999; Merino et al., 1999.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' data and citations to published literature.

claim: The enriched expression of Gdf6 may provide a complementary role to Gdf5.
source: However, the enriched expression of Gdf6 may provide a complementary role to Gdf5 [Figure 4(B); Settle et al., 2003].
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the expression pattern of Gdf6 and citation to published literature.

claim: NFATc1-expressing articular cartilage progenitors are probably a subset of GDF5+ progenitors.
source: Furthermore, based on the distribution of GDF5+ progenitors during synovial joint development and their contribution to the formation of most articular chondrocytes in previous reports Decker, 2017; Decker et al., 2017, NFATc1-expressing articular cartilage progenitors are probably a subset of GDF5+ progenitors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparing the distribution and contribution of NFATc1+ and GDF5+ cells based on the current data and published literature.

claim: Suppression of NFATc1 is sufficient to induce articular chondrogenesis both ex vivo and in vivo.
source: Our results show that suppression of NFATc1 is sufficient to induce articular chondrogenesis both ex vivo and in vivo [Figure 5(B and D–F)]
evidence: This claim is supported by CRISPR/Cas9 deletion experiments and conditional knockout data.

claim: NFATc1 could represent a core negative transcriptional regulator of articular chondrocyte differentiation.
source: and thus NFATc1 could represent a core negative transcriptional regulator of articular chondrocyte differentiation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the functional data showing NFATc1 suppresses chondrogenesis.

claim: The role of NFATc1 in regulating chondrocyte differentiation is confined to the articular cartilage because NFATc1 does not express in growth-plate progenitors or chondrocytes.
source: Notably, this role of NFATc1 in regulating chondrocyte differentiation is confined to the articular cartilage because NFATc1 does not express in growth-plate progenitors or chondrocytes [Figure 1(A and E) and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A].
evidence: This claim is inferred from the spatial expression pattern of NFATc1 shown in the data.

claim: Previous in vitro studies in murine chondrogenic cell line ATDC5 cells and human epiphyseal chondrocytes showed that NFATc1 suppresses chondrocyte differentiation.
source: Consistent with the inhibitory role of NFATc1 in articular chondrocyte differentiation, previous in vitro studies in murine chondrogenic cell line ATDC5 cells and human epiphyseal chondrocytes also showed that NFATc1 suppresses chondrocyte differentiation Zanotti and Canalis, 2013.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: A protective role of NFATc1 in osteoarthritic cartilage has been suggested based on the decrease of NFATc1 expression in lesional osteoarthritic cartilage in human patients.
source: Notably, a protective role of NFATc1 in osteoarthritic cartilage has been suggested previously, which is based on the decrease of NFATc1 expression in lesional osteoarthritic cartilage in human patients, as well as the severe articular cartilage deterioration in mice with conditional deletion of Nfatc1 driven by the Collagen 2 promoter Cre with a background of Nfatc2 deficiency (Nfatc1Col2a1;Nfatc2-/- mice) Greenblatt et al., 2013; Beier, 2014.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Nfatc1Col2a1;Nfatc2-/- mice develop osteoarthritic phenotypes.
source: While the Nfatc1Col2a1;Nfatc2-/- mice indeed develop osteoarthritic phenotypes
evidence: This claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Nfatc1AggrecanCreERT2;Nfatc2-/- mice develop obvious osteochondroma-like lesions at the entheseal site and within ligaments around the joint.
source: we did not find the typic osteoarthritic phenotype in the follow-up study in mice with deletion of Nfatc1 driven by tamoxifen-induced AggrecanCreERT2 with the background of Nfatc2 deficiency (Nfatc1AggrecanCreERT2;Nfatc2-/- mice) after administering tamoxifen at different ages. Instead, these animals develop obvious osteochondroma-like lesions at the entheseal site and within ligaments around the joint Ge et al., 2016.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The accelerated osteoarthritis phenotype in Nfatc1Col2a1;Nfatc2-/- mice could be secondary to the osteochondroma phenotype in these animals.
source: Since Col2a1 is also expressed in perichondrial precursors Akiyama et al., 2005; Ono et al., 2014, the accelerated osteoarthritis phenotype in Nfatc1Col2a1;Nfatc2-/- mice could be secondary to the osteochondroma phenotype in these animals, instead of a direct beneficial role of NFATc1 in articular cartilage.
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the expression pattern of Col2a1 and the phenotypes observed in different mouse models.

claim: A recent study by Atsuta et al. using limb bud mesenchymal cells showed that the ectopic expression of NFATc1 seems to promote chondrocyte differentiation.
source: A recent study by Atsuta et al. using limb bud mesenchymal cells showed that the ectopic expression of NFATc1 seems to promote chondrocyte differentiation as shown by the alcian blue staining in micromass-cultured cells Atsuta et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Overexpression of NFATc1 in cells from the whole limb bud might not reflect the physiological function of NFATc1 in chondrogenesis because NFATc1 expression is highly confined to articular and perichondrial progenitors during skeletal development.
source: While additional experiments are necessary to confirm chondrocyte differentiation at the molecular level, overexpression of NFATc1 in cells from the whole limb bud might not reflect the physiological function of NFATc1 in chondrogenesis because NFATc1 expression is highly confined to articular and perichondrial progenitors during skeletal development according to the lineage tracing data in Nfatc1Cre and Nfatc1CreERT2 reporter mice (Figures 1 and 2 and reference Ge et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is the authors' interpretation based on their lineage tracing data and cited reference.

claim: The disparity between the Atsuta et al. study and the current study could be due to the different cell types utilized.
source: Therefore, this disparity could also be due to the different cell types utilized in these two studies.
evidence: This claim is speculative, representing the authors' interpretation of differences between studies.

claim: A previous study showed that Notch signaling suppresses NFATc1 expression in ATDC5 cells and primary chondrocytes.
source: A previous study showed that Notch signaling suppresses NFATc1 expression in ATDC5 cells and primary chondrocytes Zanotti and Canalis, 2013.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Notch signaling can be activated by mechanical loading in mandibular condylar chondrocytes and bone marrow stromal cells.
source: Furthermore, the Notch signaling can be activated by mechanical loading in mandibular condylar chondrocytes and bone marrow stromal cells Ziouti et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2021.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: It is possible that mechanical loading and Notch signaling act upstream of NFATc1 expression during articular cartilage development.
source: Therefore, it is possible that mechanical loading and Notch signaling act upstream of NFATc1 expression during articular cartilage development.
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from published literature on Notch signaling and NFATc1.

claim: Nfatc4 is enriched in articular cartilage progenitors.
source: In addition, our transcriptome data show that Nfatc4 is also enriched in articular cartilage progenitors.
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome analysis data.

claim: Modulating NFAT signaling in skeletal progenitors may represent a novel, precise strategy for articular cartilage regeneration and treating cartilaginous diseases.
source: Given the importance of NFATc1 in articular chondrogenesis, modulating NFAT signaling in skeletal progenitors may represent a novel, precise strategy for articular cartilage regeneration and treating cartilaginous diseases.
evidence: This claim is speculative, representing the authors' interpretation of the potential therapeutic implications of their findings.
